_readme: Example config for the flake -> CIF export & placement pipeline.
1. Leave everything at these defaults and run once against flakes/all/ (or your own
already-selected images) with --no-placement to check per-image CIFs look right.
2. Inspect cif_export_results.json — any image with status 'alert' was skipped, not
3. If real markers are being missed/rejected, adjust crosshair_match_threshold and
crosshair_score_gap_min. If real flakes are missing from the output CIFs, lower
4. Confirm grid_pitch_um / placement_x_offset_um / placement_y_offset_um match your
actual marker grid and master template before trusting placement in production —
grid_pitch_um must equal the real-world spacing between adjacent grid letters
(e.g. AA to AB) on YOUR chip; do not trust a printed scale-bar overlay for this,
only the known real grid spacing.
5. Once happy, drop --no-placement and point --template at your real master CIF.
_comment_detection_config_path: DetectionConfig JSON reused for flake color range and marker pink/bright ranges — keep this in sync with whatever flake_detection used to find these images.
_comment_markers: Top-2 crosshair marker detection via template matching (no OCR) identifies WHICH two grid-dot squares are the labeled anchor markers and validates the base-case geometry. The crosshair match position itself is then discarded in favor of that square's own centroid (see square_* below) -- the crosshair template match alone was found to carry a small but systematic left/right-asymmetric bias that corrupts placement rotation/scale; the square centroid doesn't have this problem. Tune the top group if real markers are being missed (lower crosshair_match_threshold) or noise is being picked up (raise it).
_comment_squares: Grid-dot square detection -- provides the actual calibration position for each marker, via a two-pass match against square_marker_rgb (measured off a real marker's solid core), not flake_detection's much broader marker_rgb_range (which also catches part of the pale cyan/blue halo where a marker's bright color blends into the substrate, unevenly across a square's edges, skewing the centroid). Pass 1 (square_color_margin, loose) isolates each candidate blob via connected components -- has to stay loose enough to admit real per-image core-color variation without merging neighboring glyphs into one oversized blob. Pass 2 (square_core_margin, tight) recomputes each surviving blob's centroid from only the pixels in its own bounding box that tightly match the target color, excluding the halo -- safe to be tight since it only looks inside one already-isolated blob. marker_square_snap_max_distance_px (below, in the markers group) is how far a coarse crosshair match may be from a square before the image is alerted and skipped.
_comment_placement: grid_pitch_um is the ONE real-world grid used both for marker-pair calibration (scale + rotation) and for placement (grid ID -> absolute position): confirmed 200um, e.g. AA to AB. X_um = placement_x_offset_um + col_idx*grid_pitch_um, Y_um = placement_y_offset_um - row_idx*grid_pitch_um.
_comment_polygon_export: Background/foreground is separated by edge detection (Canny), not color -- immune to the substrate's lighting gradient, which tripped up every color-based approach tried before this (fixed HSV threshold, k-means clustering). edge_blur_kernel denoises before edge detection; edge_canny_low/high are the Canny hysteresis thresholds; edge_close_kernel/iterations bridge small gaps so real content's edges form closed, fillable loops. Everything inside a closed loop (flakes, debris, AND the markers/scaling marks themselves) is exported, colored by its own measured mean color. gds_min_area filters out noise contours (px) before scoring; raise it if tiny specks are showing up as polygons. min_flake_score is an OPTIONAL quality-score threshold for THIS phase (same color/texture/isolation formula as flake_detection's min_final_score, but independent of it and NOT applied by default -- flake_detection's threshold only decides which images get reviewed; this one, if raised above 0.0, decides which regions within an image get exported). Start at 0.0 (everything), inspect cif_export_results.json's polygon_scores, then raise only if you want to start excluding low-scoring regions. max_vertex_n is the CIF polygon vertex cap (larger contours are recursively split).
_comment_color_palette: Each exported polygon is colored to match its own measured color, not one fixed monocolor layer. flake_layer_palette are the 6 pre-declared 'Flake' layers (101-106) in grid_preperation/BaseGrid.cif's own layer-names header. A polygon within palette_max_distance (Euclidean RGB) of one of these reuses it; anything else (markers, debris -- not flake-colored) gets its own dynamically-allocated layer with its own color instead, quantized by palette_quantize_step so near-duplicate colors share a layer. Shared across the whole run, so the same real-world color always lands on the same layer.
_comment_output: template_cif_path is only ever read, never modified in place -- it's copied once into --output and every placement is spliced into that working copy. Set to null to skip placement entirely (same effect as --no-placement).
